subject: Pilot cutover: pass/fail signals, safety checks, and remediation playbook
messages:
From: Anna Torres <anna.torres@caravelhealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot scope and timelines - acceptance criteria request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the latency numbers looked promising. Before we kick off the pilot our engineering and procurement teams need a concise acceptance packet that we can attach to the SOW. Can you provide a one-page MAP-style acceptance checklist plus a short runnable smoke-test list that covers:

- Quantitative pass signals (how we'll measure pass/fail)
- Safety/guardrail checks (what to watch for during live traffic)
- Minimal acceptance tests our SREs can run during UAT
- Rollback/stoplight triggers for procurement

Procurement will want explicit SLA exceptions and how credits/rollback are handled if thresholds are breached. A PDF and a tiny spreadsheet of tests would be ideal.

Best,
Anna
VP Engineering, Caravel Health

Attachment: none

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Anna Torres <anna.torres@caravelhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-15T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope and timelines - acceptance criteria request

Anna — thanks, happy to send. Attaching a short MAP (MAP_v1.2.pdf) and a tiny smoke-suite spreadsheet (acceptance-tests-smoke-suite.xlsx). TL;DR summary here for quick review: 

PASS SIGNALS (required for 72 continuous hours unless otherwise noted):
- Latency: p95 inference latency < 450ms for sequences <= 512 tokens (measured by the token-meter route).
- Cost: mean token cost <= $0.0011 per generated token across observed workload.
- Quality: intent classification accuracy >= 92% on a 500-sample seeded test set (see test spreadsheet).
- Reliability: error rate (5xx + timeouts) < 0.5% of requests.

SAFETY / GUARDRAILS (monitored realtime, automatic mitigations):
- Rate limit backstop: if token throughput spikes > 2x baseline, route to reduced-capacity model variant automatically.
- Output safety: for flagged prompts (PII/PHI heuristics), redact or route to human review queue.
- Latency surge protection: if p95 > 600ms for two consecutive 5-min windows, trigger canary rollback to previous model.

MINIMAL ACCEPTANCE (UAT) SMOKE TESTS (runnable, included in spreadsheet):
1) Basic round-trip: 1000 scripted prompts, assert p95 < 450ms and error rate < 0.5%
2) Token-cost spot-check: sample 200 prompts, assert average cost below threshold
3) Intent regression: run seeded intent set (500 examples) and compute accuracy
4) Cold-start: 50 sequential cold-start requests to measure first-token latency
5) Safety checks: 100 prompts with PII heuristics to validate redaction/pathway

ROLLBACK & REMEDIATION (procurement-friendly language):
- Stoplight: Green = pass signals met; Yellow = any single pass signal marginal (within 10%); Red = any hard threshold breached (e.g., error rate >1%).
- Remediation window: For Yellow states, vendor has 24 hours to remediate; for Red, customer may pause traffic and request rollback.
- SLA credit trigger: any contiguous 24-hour period in Red on a required signal triggers a pro-rata credit (formula in PDF).

I also added a short remediation playbook and contact matrix in the PDF. Let me know if procurement wants wording changes and I can add the clause to the SOW.

Sincerely,
Soojin Lee
Commercial Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP_v1.2.pdf, acceptance-tests-smoke-suite.xlsx

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-16T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cutover materials / instrumentation notes

Picking up from Soojin's draft — a couple of practical asks from infra before we finalize: 

- Add a short check for "KV cache hit ratio" during steady-state (target >= 75%) — low cache hit drives p95 up significantly.
- Measure 1st-token latency separately from steady-state p95; include both in the spreadsheet as separate rows.
- For cost measurement, ensure tokenization is deterministic between how Caravel samples tokens and our metering route (document the tokenizer version).
- Include a heartbeat metric (route-level) so we can detect routing misconfig (e.g., wrong model variant) quickly.

I'll update the spreadsheet with these rows unless you want to own that. Also recommend a short fwd-able appendix that procurement can paste into the SOW.

-marcus
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot cutover: final MAP packet and procurement paragraph added

Anna / Procurement team — attached updated MAP_v1.2.pdf with the explicit procurement paragraph and metric retention notes. Highlights of edits: 

- Procurement paragraph (one para) now included: "If a required pass signal enters Red for a contiguous 24-hour window during the pilot, customer may elect to pause traffic to Redwood endpoints. In such an event Redwood will provide a pro-rata service credit calculated as (hours impacted / 24) * daily committed value. For Yellow states vendor will have a 24-hour remediation window; repeated Yellow states (3 occurrences in 30 days) escalate to Red treatment. All acceptance metrics used to gate pilot will be retained for 90 days for audit purposes."

- Added KV cache hit row and first-token latency row to the spreadsheet. Tokenizer version and metering route are documented in the appendix.
- SOC2 evidence link included (SOC2-evidence-link.txt) for procurement review.

Next steps:
1) Procurement to review the paragraph and confirm wording (Anna / procurement)
2) We run the smoke-suite during the internal pre-cutover on Monday (2025-09-22) and report snapshot metrics
3) If green, move to customer pilot traffic on 2025-09-23 with a 72-hour evaluation window

If that schedule works I'll also open a DocuSign envelope for the SOW with the acceptance appendix included.

Thanks,
Soojin
Commercial Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
